hero.headline: "You'll regret it if you don't!" — and your child is already saying yes?
hero.subheadline: They're being scared into acting before they think. This isn't about real consequences. It's fear manipulation.

media.alt: A child making a decision under pressure of fear about the future

pain.title: The fear of "what if it's true" makes children agree without thinking
pain.body:
"You'll regret it if you don't go", "you'll miss your chance", "it won't be there later". At school, among friends, even in ads. The child isn't sure — but the fear of "what if things really do get worse" pushes them to say yes.

This isn't about real consequences. It's fear manipulation: someone deliberately uses the future to scare the child into acting immediately rather than thinking. When scared, the brain doesn't check facts — it just wants to remove the discomfort fast.

The result — the child agrees to things that aren't right for them, just to avoid "something worse". They don't realise they were deliberately scared — or that in most cases, there would have been nothing to regret at all.

faq.q: Is it a game or a learning course?
faq.a: Both at the same time. "Sila Slova" looks like a detective series, but every episode contains a hidden critical thinking lesson.

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideal for 8–12 year olds. At this age, children are most receptive to new thinking patterns and haven't yet formed rigid biases.

faq.q: How much time is needed each day?
faq.a: 15–20 minutes per episode. Flexible schedule — your child can come back at any convenient time.

faq.q: Is registration required for the demo?
faq.a: No. The demo episode is fully open — no registration, no subscription, no personal data required.
